correctness.rationale: PASS: The tight Gram is equivalent after normalization to vanishing Fourier moments k=1,2,3 and conjugates. Any alleged rule at <=5 nodes can be zero-extended to five distinct 2p-th roots, with P=product(z-z_j). The Laurent polynomials z^-2 P, z^-3P supported in [-3,3] and vanish at nodes; their constant coefficients force e3=e2=0. Express each root as epsilon_j zeta_p^rj: e2=0 gives integer pair-sum coefficients c_r all equal by Phi_p=1+...+z^(p-1), hence pc=((sum epsilon)^2-5)/2 in {-2,2,10}, impossible for p>=7. For six roots, choose three pth roots with angular gaps <pi (residues 0,floor(p/3),ceil(2p/3)); strict positive barycentric weights cancel second moments while antipodal pairing kills first and third. Checked independent positive moment residual for 13 primes through p=103, all small <3e-13; the cyclotomic argument, not enumeration, proves infinite p.
